newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 18.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
NARAYANAN ELECTED PRESIDENT

Vice president Kocheril Raman Narayanan was Thursday declared elected president of India, becoming the first from a low Hindu caste to get elected to the job. He polled 95 percent of the valid votes. His sole opponent T.N.Seshan, a former chief election commissioner, lost his security deposit in the election. Narayanan, 76, will be sworn in as president for five years on July 25. In the Indian presidential election votes are cast by the members of parliament and the members of the state legislative assemblies through a system of proportional voting. Of the 4,471 valid votes, Narayanan polled 4,231 votes while his opponent polled 240 votes.
The Hindustan Times
RULING FRONT DECIDES TO KEEP YADAV'S PARTY OUT

The ruling United Front leaders Thursday night decided not to admit the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) party of Bihar Chief Minister Laloo Yadav into the Front. The standing committee of the United Front said Laloo Yadav should resign as chief minister but did not say anything about dismissing his government. The regional Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party decided not to press with its threat earlier in the week to withdraw from the government in protest against squabbles in the coalition.
The Economic Times
NEW SEA POLICY LIMITS FOREIGN LINER OPERATIONS

The first comprehensive draft national shipping policy disallows foreign liners from transporting liquefied natural gas and liquefied petroleum gas. They are also prevented from costal shipping operations. Only fully-owned overseas subsidiaries of Indian companies or Indian subsidiaries of overseas shipping companies having a minimum of five vessels will be allowed coastal shipping. The draft proposes to give income tax relief to Indian seafarers and subsidy to private and government shipyards. It also gives infrastructure status to coastal shipping and export industry status to overseas shipping. The draft was approved by a ministerial committee on Thursday.
BAN ON DIRECT TO HOME SERVICES CONFIRMED

The government re-issued on Thursday a notification banning direct-to-home (DTH) satellite broadcasts it had withdrawn minutes after issue on Wednesday. The notification says the government will not allow reception of services on 4,800 MHz and above. But no licence is needed to receive services being transmitted through C-band transponders. The secretary of the Information and Broadcasting Ministry said the objective of the ban was to insure that nobody should make a preemptive entry before the setting up of a broadcasting authority.
PRIVATE PARTIES CAN OWN SATELLITES

The government has decided to allow private companies to have commercial communication satellites and offered government satellites' transponders for non-government use. A press release by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) said its Insat system would be offered to non-governmental users on commercial terms subject to the capacity available. Indian private parties will be allowed to establish commercial communication satellites and the parties will be assisted in registering such satellite systems and networks with the International Telecommunications Union as Indian satellites.
Financial Express
FINANCE FIRMS EASING DEBT-EQUITY RATIO

Long term lending institutions have started relaxing the debt equity ratios in virtually every industrial sector to prop up project financing. They are also reappraising projects against the backdrop of a sudden dip in the interest rates. A senior executive of the Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) said lenders were relaxing the debt-equity ratio selectively. Institutional sources said in the second half of fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) a clutch of primary issues will hit the market with realistic pricing. They attributed the current situation to bad pricing of issues. A few corporates have started privately placing equity issues with institutions to tide over the crisis.
SCOTIABANK TO ENTER INDIA

Scotiabank which is one of the largest banks in Canada is setting up a non-banking finance company (NBFC) in India. It will bring in 75 percent equity. The remaining equity will come from its local partner. The bank also plans to manage the activities of mutual funds in future through a 100 percent subsidiary of the proposed NBFC. The Foreign Investment Promotion Board has cleared the proposal. The NBFC will have a minimum capital of $6.67 millions of which $5.0 million will come from Scotiabank. The fund will be infused through its subsidiaries or associates in Bahamas, Mauritius or elsewhere.
Business Standard
RESERVE BANK SIGNALS LOWER INTEREST RATES

The Reserve Bank increased the sale price of gilts at its counter in its open market operations twice on Thursday signalling lower interest rates. Open market operations have been used four times since July 12 and each time yields have been lowered. By varying the prices of the security it puts on its sale-purchase window the Reserve Bank can send interest rate impulses into the financial system. The Bank governor said the bank rate and its open market operations would be extensively used as a signal to indicate its objectives regarding interest rates.
The Observer
OILSEEDS EXPORT BROUGHT UNDER LICENCE

The government has brought the export of sesame seed, sunflower seed, rapeseed and mustard seed under its licensing scheme with effect from July 14. A notification by the director general of foreign trade said seeds and planting material of all kinds were permitted under licences. Exporters are unhappy over the new policy. Export of sesame seeds under licence would result in invariable bureaucratic delays and uncertainties which would shake the confidence of overseas buyers about regular supplies from India, they say.
IMF WANTS INDIA TO RISE PETRO PRICES

The International Monitory Fund (IMF) has urged India to increase the prices of petroleum products substantially as part of a larger effort at fiscal consolidation and structural reforms. An IMF statement said the gross domestic product rose by 6.5 percent in fiscal 1996/97 9 (April-March) and averaged nearly seven percent over the last three years. It recommended a substantial increase in petroleum product prices, a more flexible exchange rate management, an exit policy to help the closure of ailing companies, privatisation of state-owned firms, removal of remaining import quota barriers on consumer goods and reduction of reservation for the small scale sector.
MORE GOVERNMENT COMPANIES TO GET AUTONOMY

The government has drawn up a second list of its companies to be given autonomy. These companies will have a lesser degree of autonomy than that was given to nine government companies recently. The restrictions will be in matters of incuring capital expenditure, in forming financial joint ventures and in raising debt from capital markets. But they will enjoy full operational freedom.
Business Line
OMNIBUS GUARANTEE ON THE CARDS

The government is considering a proposal to provide "omnibus" guarantee to infrastructure projects which will do away with going into the details of each project separately. It is also planning to replace the counter-guarantee system in the power sector with a quicker process. A discussion paper prepared by the Industry Ministry said the important constraint in infrastructure funding both in the domestic and international markets was the issue of government guarantees. The paper said the government was taking a long time to give guarantees to the fast track power projects and it taxed the patience of investors and lenders.
